thm003: Let n > 1 be a natural number.
If n is prime, then n itself is a prime factor of n.
By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic,
n can be written as a product of prime numbers: n = p₁p₂...pₖ
Therefore, p₁ is a prime factor of n
Thus, every n > 1 has at least one prime factor.

thm005: Let a, b, c be positive real numbers such that a² + b² = c²
Consider a triangle with sides a, b, c
By the converse of the Pythagorean theorem:
If the sides of a triangle satisfy a² + b² = c²
Then the triangle is a right triangle
Therefore, a, b, c form a right triangle

thm007: By group axioms, G must have an identity element e
